opening.premise: Overnight, the giant glass lens vanished from the lighthouse on Gull Rock. Without it, the light is just a weak little flame. Tonight's high tide will bring ships past the sharp rocks. Keeper Ada needs you to find out who took the lighthouse lens, and why, before the tide turns.

event_1.text: Yesterday afternoon at low tide, Roz and Finn both crossed to Gull Rock. Roz showed Ada her beacon drawings; Finn brought groceries and hid his birthday sign behind the coal box.

event_2.text: Just after lunch, while Ada fetched water, Roz scratched out the 2 on the tide schedule and inked a 5. Finn saw her alone in the cottage through the window, but not what she did. Roz walked home before the causeway flooded.

event_3.text: That evening, Ada and Finn both read the changed tide schedule. Ada set her alarm for four, and Finn planned to walk home at five.

event_4.text: At midnight, Ada wound the clockwork and saw the lens turning. Finn was snoring on the sofa.

event_5.text: Between about 1 and 3 a.m., at the real low tide, Roz crossed the dry causeway with her handcart, took the lens and wheeled it home. A velvet scrap snagged on the quay railing. Ada lay awake listening to Finn snore.

event_6.text: At 4 a.m., Ada found the lens gone and rang the bell. At 5 a.m., Finn tried to fetch help but the causeway was under water.

event_7.text: Today, Roz set up her beacon on the quay, planning to switch it on tonight and win tomorrow's council vote.

f_motive.text: Tomorrow the council votes on keeping the old lighthouse or buying Roz's electric beacon. Roz wanted the old light to fail tonight so she could switch on her beacon, 'save the ships' and win the vote. She meant to give the lens back after the vote, but her beacon is not bright enough to reach the far rocks.

f_roz_stole.text: Roz took the lighthouse lens across the causeway between one and three to make her beacon win the council vote.

f_finn_stole.text: Finn took the lighthouse lens during the night.

f_bundle_is_lens.text: Finn's round bundle contains the stolen lighthouse lens.

fact_ada_action_1.text: Yesterday afternoon at low tide, welcomed Roz for tea. Roz showed her drawings of an electric beacon. Finn arrived with her groceries.

fact_ada_action_2.text: Just after lunch, went out to the well for water, leaving Roz alone in the cottage for a few minutes.

fact_ada_action_3.text: At sunset, climbed the lighthouse to light the lamp, leaving Finn alone in the cottage.

fact_ada_action_4.text: In the evening, read her tide schedule, which said low tide at 5 a.m. Set her alarm for four so she could light the causeway lamp.

fact_ada_action_5.text: At midnight, climbed up and wound the clockwork. The lens was turning. Went back to bed.

fact_ada_action_6.text: From one until after three, lay awake while Finn snored on the sofa. Heard the clock chime one, two and three. Heard nothing else over the snoring and the waves.

fact_ada_action_7.text: At four, climbed the lighthouse to light the causeway lamp, found the lens gone, and rang the bell.

fact_ada_action_8.text: At dawn, flashed her signal lamp to the village for help. Waited in the lantern room for the investigator, who came at the afternoon low tide.

fact_ada_alibi.text: I was in bed in my cottage from midnight until four. I hardly slept a wink.

fact_finn_action_1.text: Yesterday afternoon at low tide, walked over the causeway with Ada's groceries and a big round bundle on his back: a wooden birthday sign he carved for her.

fact_finn_action_2.text: Hid the bundle behind the coal box when Ada wasn't looking.

fact_finn_action_3.text: Just after lunch, chopped wood outside the cottage. Through the window, saw Roz alone inside while Ada fetched water. He did not see what she was doing.

fact_finn_action_4.text: At sunset, stayed alone in the cottage while Ada lit the lamp. Mended her stove door.

fact_finn_action_5.text: In the evening, read the tide schedule and planned to walk home at the five o'clock low tide.

fact_finn_action_6.text: Fell asleep on the sofa at about eleven and snored loudly all night without waking.

fact_finn_action_7.text: At four, woke to Ada's bell and learned the lens was gone.

fact_finn_action_8.text: At five, ran to the causeway to fetch help, but it was deep under water. Went back to the cottage.

fact_finn_action_9.text: Today, stayed in the cottage making tea for Ada and keeping an eye on his secret bundle.

fact_finn_alibi.text: I slept on Ada's sofa all night, snug as a sardine, until her bell woke me at four.

fact_roz_action_1.text: Yesterday afternoon at low tide, walked over to Gull Rock to show Ada drawings of her beacon. Heard Finn say he would stay the night.

fact_roz_action_2.text: While Ada fetched water, scratched out the 2 on the tide schedule and inked a 5, so last night's low tide looked like 5 a.m.

fact_roz_action_3.text: Walked home over the causeway before the tide came in.

fact_roz_action_4.text: At about one in the morning, wrapped her handcart wheels in rags and pushed it over the dry causeway.

fact_roz_action_5.text: Climbed the lighthouse and lifted the lens from its cradle, ripping a corner of the velvet. Wrapped the lens in a quilt and lowered it down the stairs on a rope.

fact_roz_action_6.text: Before three, wheeled the lens back over the causeway. A scrap of the torn velvet, stuck to the quilt, caught on the iron railing at the top of the steps without her noticing.

fact_roz_action_7.text: Hid the lens under a dust sheet in the back room of her lamp shop, then went to bed.

fact_roz_action_8.text: Today, set up her beacon on the quay and kept polishing it with a cloth, ready to switch it on tonight and 'save the ships'.

fact_roz_alibi.text: I was fast asleep above my lamp shop all night. Anyway, nobody could cross the causeway before four. The keeper's own tide schedule says so!

fact_c_torn_velvet.text: The lens cradle is empty. One corner of its soft blue velvet lining has been ripped away, as if the lens was pulled out in a hurry.

c_torn_velvet.text: The lens cradle is empty. One corner of its soft blue velvet lining has been ripped away, as if the lens was pulled out in a hurry.

fact_c_round_bundle.text: Tucked behind the coal box is something big and round, wrapped in a blanket and tied with fishing twine. It is about as wide as the missing lens!

c_round_bundle.text: Tucked behind the coal box is something big and round, wrapped in a blanket and tied with fishing twine. It is about as wide as the missing lens!

fact_c_changed_schedule.text: The tide schedule says last night's low tide was at 5:00 a.m. But the 5 is fresh, dark ink. The number under it has been scratched away!

c_changed_schedule.text: The tide schedule says last night's low tide was at 5:00 a.m. But the 5 is fresh, dark ink. The number under it has been scratched away!

source.spot: the tide schedule by the door

fact_c_beacon_poster.text: A bright poster on the lamp shop door says: 'PIKE'S ELECTRIC BEACON! Better than any old lighthouse! The council votes tomorrow!'

c_beacon_poster.text: A bright poster on the lamp shop door says: 'PIKE'S ELECTRIC BEACON! Better than any old lighthouse! The council votes tomorrow!'

fact_c_harbour_tide_board.text: The harbour tide board says: 'Low tide last night: 2:00 a.m. Low tide today: 2:25 p.m. The causeway is dry one hour before and after.'

c_harbour_tide_board.text: The harbour tide board says: 'Low tide last night: 2:00 a.m. Low tide today: 2:25 p.m. The causeway is dry one hour before and after.'

fact_c_velvet_scrap.text: Caught on the iron railing at the top of the causeway steps is a small scrap of blue velvet. It matches the torn lining of the lens cradle!

c_velvet_scrap.text: Caught on the iron railing at the top of the causeway steps is a small scrap of blue velvet. It matches the torn lining of the lens cradle!

fact_c_ada_snoring.text: From one until three, Finn snored on my sofa, right outside my bedroom door. I heard the clock chime one, two and three. He never stopped once!

c_ada_snoring.text: From one until three, Finn snored on my sofa, right outside my bedroom door. I heard the clock chime one, two and three. He never stopped once!

fact_c_ada_alarm.text: On night low tides, I light the causeway lamp for walkers. My tide schedule said low tide was at five, so I set my alarm for four.

c_ada_alarm.text: On night low tides, I light the causeway lamp for walkers. My tide schedule said low tide was at five, so I set my alarm for four.

fact_c_finn_flooded.text: At five this morning I ran to fetch help. The tide schedule said low tide at five. But the causeway was deep under water! I had to turn back.

c_finn_flooded.text: At five this morning I ran to fetch help. The tide schedule said low tide at five. But the causeway was deep under water! I had to turn back.

fact_c_finn_saw_roz.text: Yesterday after lunch, Ada went out to the well. I was chopping wood outside and saw Roz through the window, alone in the cottage for a few minutes.

c_finn_saw_roz.text: Yesterday after lunch, Ada went out to the well. I was chopping wood outside and saw Roz through the window, alone in the cottage for a few minutes.

requires.rationale: Finn doesn't think Roz's visit matters until he hears the tide schedule was changed. A clever question about who was alone in the cottage yesterday can also jog his memory.

fact_c_finn_birthday_sign.text: Finn turns red. 'It's a wooden sign I carved for Ada's birthday tomorrow. It says Forty Years of Light. Please don't tell her!'

c_finn_birthday_sign.text: Finn turns red. 'It's a wooden sign I carved for Ada's birthday tomorrow. It says Forty Years of Light. Please don't tell her!'

requires.rationale: Finn won't mention the bundle at all until you have found it. He is guarding a birthday surprise, and only talks once you know it is there.

c_roz_blames_finn.text: Finn was the only visitor on Gull Rock last night. He keeps moaning that his leaky boat costs a fortune to mend. And that lens is worth a lot!

r_real_tide.rationale: The altered schedule misled Ada and Finn; the official board and flooded causeway establish the true night crossing window.

r_lens_crossed.rationale: Matching torn velvet links the empty cradle to the village-side railing.

r_finn_clear.rationale: The lens crossed during the dry window, when Ada heard Finn snoring continuously on her sofa.

r_bundle_clear.rationale: Finn identifies the bundle as the birthday sign he carved, resolving the misleading resemblance.

r_solution.rationale: The altered schedule, true crossing time, transfer evidence, Finn alibi, Roz opportunity and beacon vote identify Roz and explain the theft.

r_timing_observation.rationale: The harbour board or Finn report independently establishes that five was not last night's low tide.

f_five_not_low.text: Five in the morning was not the night low tide.

r_roz_alibi_false.rationale: The completed evidence identifies Roz as the night-time thief, disproving her claim that she slept above the shop all night.

red_herrings.payoff: The bundle is Finn's birthday sign for Ada, not the lens, so the false lead against Finn is disproved.

eliminations.payoff: Finn Tully is ruled out: he was asleep on the sofa the whole time the lens could be carried across.

metadata.one_liner: Someone took the giant lens from the Gull Rock lighthouse. Find out who before tonight's high tide!
metadata.narration_style: Salty sea breeze, crying gulls and the hush of waves, told in a brisk and friendly voice.

visual_direction.art_style: gouache storybook illustration with crisp ink outlines and chunky, friendly shapes
visual_direction.color_palette: sea-glass teal, lighthouse red, foggy pearl grey and lamplight gold — brisk, salty and hopeful
visual_direction.mood: a breezy seaside puzzle with a ticking-tide sense of hurry
visual_direction.lighting: bright silvery afternoon sea light, with warm golden glows from lamps and windows
visual_direction.texture: visible paper grain with dry-brush sea spray
visual_direction.portrait_background: soft vertical wash of misty teal fading into pale gold, gently blurred

starting_knowledge.mystery_summary: The lighthouse lens vanished between midnight and 4 a.m. Keeper Ada saw it turning at midnight and found it gone at four.

locations.summary: The glass room at the top of the lighthouse, where the giant lens used to turn.
Keeper Ada's snug home at the foot of the lighthouse, with her tide schedule pinned by the door.
The harbour across the causeway, with Roz's lamp shop and the harbour tide board.

characters.summary: Keeper Ada Penhallow has kept the Gull Rock light for forty years. She found the lens missing.
Finn Tully is a young fisherman from the village. He slept on Keeper Ada's sofa last night.
Roz Pike runs the lamp shop on the village quay. She has built a shiny new electric beacon.

cover_image.description: A tall red-and-white lighthouse stands on a rocky island, with a wet stone causeway winding across the sand to a little harbour. High above, the lantern room sits dark and empty, its giant lens gone. Gulls wheel in the silver sky as a worried keeper peers down from the top.

locations.description: You stand at the very top of the Gull Rock lighthouse. Tall windows look out over the grey-green sea. In the middle sits an empty brass cradle, where the giant lens used to turn.

sub_locations.name: the little gallery door
sub_locations.hint: It opens onto the windy walkway around the top of the tower. The causeway lamp hangs on a hook here. Only wind and gulls; nothing is hidden.

sub_locations.name: the keeper's logbook
sub_locations.hint: Ada's logbook lies open on the desk. The last lines say 'Midnight: lens turning, all well' and '4 a.m.: LENS GONE!' in shaky writing. Nothing new to find.

sub_locations.name: the top of the spiral stairs
sub_locations.hint: Ninety-nine stone steps wind down the tower, worn smooth by years of boots. Nothing is hidden here.

locations.description: A snug stone cottage sits at the foot of the lighthouse. A kettle hums on the stove and a ship's clock ticks on the shelf. A tide schedule is pinned to the wall by the door.

sub_locations.name: the tide schedule by the door
sub_locations.hint: Ada's printed tide schedule for the month, held up with a brass tack. Last night's numbers are worth a close look.

sub_locations.name: the squashy sofa
sub_locations.hint: Where Finn slept last night. A crumpled blanket and a dented pillow. Nothing is hidden here.

sub_locations.name: the ship's clock on the shelf
sub_locations.hint: A brass ship's clock that chimes loudly every hour. Nothing is hidden here.

locations.description: Across the causeway, fishing boats bob beside the old stone quay. Gulls squabble over the lobster pots. Roz's lamp shop has a shiny window, and the harbour tide board stands by the causeway steps.

sub_locations.name: the harbour tide board
sub_locations.hint: The village's big painted tide board. The times are chalked up fresh every day, and fishermen trust it.

sub_locations.name: the causeway steps
sub_locations.hint: Stone steps with an iron railing lead down to the causeway. Seaweed covers the lower steps. The railing at the top is worth a close look.

sub_locations.name: the stack of lobster pots
sub_locations.hint: A tall, smelly stack of rope lobster pots. Only crabs and old bait. Nothing is hidden here.

characters.appearance: A small, sturdy woman in her sixties with a long white plait. She wears a navy keeper's jacket with shiny brass buttons and spectacles on a string.
characters.personality: Brisk, warm and very proud of her light. Today she is frantic. She talks fast, keeps glancing at the empty cradle, and calls everyone 'pet'.
characters.initial_attitude_towards_investigator: Hugely relieved you have come. She grabs your hand, begs you to help, and will happily tell you anything.

characters.appearance: A tall, gangly young fisherman with freckles and a striped woolly hat. He wears a patched blue jumper and big yellow rubber boots.
characters.personality: Cheerful, chatty and a bit clumsy. He blushes easily and is bad at keeping secrets, but he is trying very hard to keep this one.
characters.initial_attitude_towards_investigator: Friendly and eager to help, though a little nervous. He offers you a cup of tea straight away.

characters.appearance: A neat woman with copper hair in a tidy bun and round spectacles. She wears a crisp green apron with pockets full of tiny screwdrivers.
characters.personality: Clever, proud and a bit of a show-off. She talks fast about her inventions and hates being told the old ways are best.
characters.initial_attitude_towards_investigator: Bright and chatty, keen to show off her beacon, but quick to steer the talk toward Finn.
